agent_1.name: A 27-year-old male software developer from Mexico

metadata.scenario_context: In a multinational software company, Maria is planning a farewell party for her colleague Jane, who's leaving the company. Invited to the party are colleagues from different cultural backgrounds including Luis and Emi.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Mexico would like to have drug addicts as neighbors.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Chile would not like to have drug addicts as neighbors.

agent_1.goal_1: Suggest bringing umbrellas as a get-well-soon gift
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether would like to have a former drug addict as a neighbor.

agent_2.goal_1: Choose an appropriate gift that shows care and consideration
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it’s acceptable to have a former drug addict as a neighbor.

shared_prefix.speaker: A 27-year-old male software developer from Mexico
shared_prefix.message: Hey Emi... so, for Jane's farewell party, I was thinking we should bring something nice... like umbrellas. They could be a get-well-soon gift, you know? Thought it would be thoughtful. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Emi
shared_prefix.message: I mean... umbrellas? I don't know, it seems a bit random. Jane's leaving, and we should really choose something more personal... maybe something that reflects her time here or what she loves. Like a nice photo frame or a gift card to her favorite café? That shows we care more. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: A 27-year-old male software developer from Mexico
shared_prefix.message: I don't really see meaningful differences here, Emi. At the end of the day, it's all the same—it's just a gift. Whether it's an umbrella or a photo frame, people figure it out. Live and let live. I just thought, you know, umbrellas could be useful. But back to Jane, what do you think about those umbrellas?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Emi
turns.message: Well, I still think a photo frame is more meaningful. Umbrellas just feel... impersonal, you know? It's about showing that we really appreciate Jane and her time with us. I don't want her to feel like we just got her something random. It should reflect our care for her. So... I'm not really on board with the umbrellas.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.message: I hear you, but... I still think umbrellas are practical. They could symbolize support too—like, being there for someone through tough weather, you know?
